content: The effects of weather and climate change on the transmission of dengue fever have been extensively studied, with findings published in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases in 2013. These studies highlight the influence of environmental factors on the abundance and activity of Aedes aegypti mosquitoes, the primary vector for dengue virus transmission. Guidance on determining the target difference and conducting sample size calculations for randomized controlled trials was provided in a 2018 BMJ publication. This guidance is critical for ensuring the statistical validity and reliability of clinical trials. Research on the relationship between entomological indicators of Aedes aegypti abundance and dengue virus infection was published in 2017 in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases. This study emphasized the importance of monitoring mosquito populations to predict and control dengue outbreaks. A rapid quality control test to support the development of genetic control methods in mosquitoes was introduced in a 2018 Scientific Reports article. This innovation aims to enhance the effectiveness of genetic strategies for mosquito population management. The longevity of mass-reared, irradiated, and packaged male Anopheles arabiensis and Aedes aegypti mosquitoes under simulated environmental field conditions was evaluated in a 2018 study published in Parasites & Vectors. This research is essential for optimizing the sterile insect technique (SIT) for vector control. The second edition of Introduction to Insect Biology and Diversity, published in 1998, provides foundational knowledge on insect biology, including the ecological and economic importance of various insect species. The effectiveness of mass trapping using BG-Sentinel traps for dengue vector control was evaluated in a cluster randomized controlled trial conducted in Manaus, Brazil, and published in the Journal of Medical Entomology in 2014. This study demonstrated the potential of targeted trapping strategies in reducing mosquito populations. The use of adult mosquitoes to transfer insecticides to Aedes aegypti larval habitats was explored in a 2009 study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. This innovative approach leverages mosquito behavior to enhance larval control efforts. The calculation of disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) to quantify the burden of disease was discussed in a 2014 publication in the International Journal of Public Health. This metric is crucial for evaluating the impact of diseases and the effectiveness of public health interventions. A small-scale release of genetically modified sterile male mosquitoes for malaria control was conducted in Burkina Faso, as reported by Target Malaria in 2019. This pilot study represents a significant step toward the use of genetic technologies in vector control. The economic evaluation of health care programs, including vector control interventions, was detailed in the 2005 book Methods for the Economic Evaluation of Health Care Programmes by Drummond et al. This resource provides a framework for assessing the cost-effectiveness of public health strategies. The principles and practices of the sterile insect technique (SIT) in area-wide integrated pest management were comprehensively reviewed in a 2006 book edited by Dyck and Robinson. This publication serves as a key reference for implementing SIT programs. A scoping review on vector-borne diseases in urban areas, published in 2018 in Infectious Diseases of Poverty, examined transmission dynamics, vectorial capacity, and co-infection risks. This review underscores the complexity of controlling vector-borne diseases in densely populated settings. The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) has published numerous guidelines and standards for the export, shipment, import, and release of biological control agents, as well as for the quality control of sterile mass-reared insects. These documents are essential for ensuring the safe and effective implementation of biological control programs. The use of insecticide-treated curtains and water container covers for dengue vector control was evaluated in cluster randomized trials conducted in Mexico and Venezuela, with findings published in the BMJ in 2006. These interventions demonstrated significant reductions in mosquito populations and dengue transmission. The laboratory evaluation of the effects of sterilizing doses of gamma rays on the flight activity and performance of Aedes albopictus males was published in PLoS One in 2018. This study provides insights into the potential impacts of irradiation on mosquito behavior and competitiveness. Dengue virus surveillance for early warning systems was implemented in Singapore, as reported in Emerging Infectious Diseases in 2010. This approach highlights the importance of real-time monitoring for outbreak prevention and control. The sterile insect technique (SIT) as a strategy against mosquito disease vectors was revisited in a 2015 article in Current Opinion in Insect Science. This review emphasized the potential of SIT in reducing mosquito populations and disease transmission. The first proof-of-concept study to suppress Aedes aegypti populations in semi-rural settings in Thailand was published in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases in 2019. This study demonstrated the feasibility of integrated vector control strategies in reducing mosquito densities. The suppression of dengue transmission through integrated vector control strategies at sero-positive GIS-based foci was reported in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2008. This study highlights the importance of targeted interventions in high-risk areas. The economic importance of insects and their role in various ecosystems were discussed in the 1997 book The Economic Importance of Insects by Hill. This publication provides a comprehensive overview of the benefits and challenges associated with insect populations. The evaluation of PICO as a knowledge representation for clinical questions was presented in the AMIA Annual Symposium Proceedings in 2006. This framework facilitates the systematic formulation and analysis of clinical research questions. The quality control for expanded tsetse production, sterilization, and field application was detailed in an IAEA publication in 2012. This document provides guidelines for ensuring the effectiveness of SIT programs for tsetse fly control. The model business plan for a sterile insect production facility, published by the IAEA in 2008, outlines the operational and financial considerations for establishing and managing SIT facilities. The use of genetically modified mosquitoes for vector control was addressed in a 2017 scientific opinion by the High Council for Biotechnology in France. This report provides a comprehensive assessment of the risks and benefits associated with genetic technologies in vector control. The systematic review of community-based dengue control programs, published in 2007 in the Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene, evaluated the achievements and challenges of these initiatives. This review highlights the importance of community engagement in vector control efforts. The radiation biology of mosquitoes was explored in a 2009 publication, providing insights into the effects of irradiation on mosquito physiology and behavior. This research is critical for optimizing SIT programs. The stepped wedge cluster randomized trial design was reviewed in a 2015 BMJ article, which discussed its rationale, design, analysis, and reporting. This trial design is particularly useful for evaluating public health interventions. The acceptability of non-mesh, long-lasting insecticidal nets among nomadic communities in Kenya was investigated in a 2015 study published in Malaria Journal. This research highlights the importance of cultural and contextual factors in the adoption of vector control tools.
